title: Why a product record is more useful than another sales message
body:
A product record gives the same buying information a stable home. That matters when a seller is answering several conversations about one item: a price in one chat, dimensions in another and a photograph somewhere else are difficult to keep consistent.

### What the product screen actually brings together
The inspected oBizee product editor includes the product name, description, price, images and category. It also distinguishes a straightforward product from one with selectable combinations. These fields organise information; they do not verify that a photograph, description or price is accurate.

For a handmade coaster, explain whether the price buys one piece or a set. State the size and material, show the actual item, and choose a category a buyer would recognise. This is an illustrative preparation example, not a merchant result.

### When this helps—and when it does not
Use a product record for information that should remain consistent between buyers. Keep a genuinely bespoke agreement separate until the specification is settled. A saved description should not silently replace a customer-specific commitment.

Before sharing the product, compare its buyer-facing presentation with the saved record. Check the unit being sold, images and selectable prices. Saving successfully is not the same as completing that check.

### Next step
Use the product-catalogue feature guide for capability details. The related help article owns the exact setup steps; this explanation is about deciding what belongs in the record.

title: Product options should identify the exact item a customer buys
body:
“Blue, medium” needs to identify a real combination, not merely decorate a description. If colour and size influence availability or price, a buyer needs to choose them explicitly.

### Combinations, not loose labels
The inspected oBizee editor handles option definitions alongside individual combinations with their own values. A selection is therefore more than text that happens to appear in a chat. The product form also contains handling for older option data; that is not evidence that every historical catalogue is ready without checking.

Consider a shirt available in two sizes and two colours. List the combinations you actually sell. Do not imply that all four exist merely because both size names and both colour names appear.

### Separate price evidence from presentation
A product-level price is not enough to demonstrate what each combination will cost. Check the selected combination in the storefront and carry that same choice into the bag. Use distinctive names rather than internal shorthand customers cannot interpret.

### A useful evaluation
Prepare one product with the most demanding real combinations in your range. Verify labels, image associations and prices before editing the rest of the catalogue. This is a controlled suitability check, not a promise that options eliminate every inventory mistake. The options feature page owns the detailed capability explanation.

title: Categories are customer navigation, not your stockroom filing system
body:
A category is useful when it helps someone choose where to look next. Internal production labels can organise your work without making sense to a first-time customer.

### The supported distinction
The inspected merchant source includes category listing and category creation/editing surfaces. Treat these as catalogue organisation tools. They do not prove automated categorisation, search-demand research or category-image generation.

A gift shop might separate gift sets from individual accessories because that distinction changes the purchase. Dividing every colour into a new category may instead scatter related choices. This is a merchandising decision, not a rule that one category structure always wins.

### Test the route, not just the name
Place a representative product in the intended category and inspect the customer-facing destination. Ask whether the category name matches what is inside. Check products with similar names so a buyer does not mistake a collection for a specific item.

### Keep the structure maintainable
A category should earn its place through useful products and a clear buying reason. Empty or ambiguous categories add decisions without adding help. Review the structure when the catalogue changes; do not promise improved rankings or sales simply because more categories exist.

The category-navigation feature page and related setup guide cover the supported controls. This article supplies the customer-facing decision behind them.

title: Stock tracking starts with a count you can explain
body:
Turning on stock tracking does not establish how many units are really available. The starting number must come from a count whose boundaries are understood.

### What the control asks for
The inspected tracking control asks for an initial stock quantity and a minimum stock level. Its validation rejects a minimum above the initial quantity. That is a form rule, not a recommendation to choose an unrealistically low warning threshold.

Before entering a number, decide how damaged pieces, reserved orders and unfinished work are treated. For a handmade product, raw materials are not automatically finished units. A count that mixes those states can look precise while remaining unusable.

### Record the starting position
Choose a count time and keep a short note of what was included. Check the saved item afterward. When products have combinations, confirm the quantity belongs to the intended combination rather than assuming a total applies to every option.

### What not to conclude
A tracking switch is not proof of synchronisation with every marketplace, protection against all concurrent orders or a replenishment forecast. Those claims need separate evidence.

Use the stock-tracking feature page for supported behaviour, then the setup help for the exact action. The aim is a defensible baseline that later movements can be compared against.

title: A stock adjustment needs a reason, not just a new number
body:
When the shelf and the screen disagree, changing the number is only part of the repair. Someone should later be able to understand why the change was made.

### What the adjustment records
The inspected adjustment form separates adding from subtracting stock, requires a positive adjustment quantity and asks for a reason. It also checks whether the proposed subtraction would produce negative stock. These controls make the action more explicit; they do not investigate the discrepancy for you.

“Damaged during packing: one unit removed” is more useful than “fix.” Do not include customer phone numbers or payment details in an inventory note. The explanation should identify the operational event with no unnecessary personal information.

### Check the target
Confirm the product or combination before submitting. An accurate quantity applied to the wrong item leaves two discrepancies instead of one. Compare the resulting balance with the count you intended to record.

### Avoid using adjustments as a substitute for investigation
Repeated unexplained corrections may indicate a process problem: unrecorded offline sales, inconsistent reservations or counting unfinished goods as finished stock. Review the sequence rather than repeatedly overwriting its result.

The stock-history feature page is the owning capability page. This explainer focuses on why a meaningful adjustment reason is part of the record, not optional administrative decoration.

title: Low-stock attention is a signal to investigate, not an automatic purchase order
body:
A low-stock list helps decide where to look first. It cannot independently tell you how much to make or buy.

### What the evidence supports
The inspected application includes a dedicated low-stock screen alongside inventory management. That supports an explanation of an attention workflow. It does not establish supplier ordering, demand forecasting or notification delivery through every channel.

When an item appears low, first check whether the quantity is correct. Then consider outstanding work, supplier lead time and whether the product is still part of your active range. A seasonal item and a steady seller may need very different responses at the same quantity.

### Use a realistic threshold
The warning level should leave enough time to act under your own operating conditions. Keep the reasoning outside the feature promise: the software can display a threshold-related state without knowing your production schedule.

### Close the operational loop
Record the action you chose and revisit the item after stock changes. If no action is needed, know why. Do not equate disappearance from a list with proof that a supplier delivery arrived.

Use the low-stock feature page to understand the supported surface and the related help guide to find it. Reordering decisions remain a separate business judgement.

title: Stock history is most useful when you read a sequence
body:
One balance tells you where a record stands. A movement history helps explain how it got there.

### Start with a question
The inspected application contains a stock transaction history screen. Use a question such as “Why did this item change after yesterday’s count?” rather than treating the list as a report that explains itself.

Compare a known starting point, the recorded movements and the ending position. Where a note is unclear, investigate its underlying event. Do not invent a cause from a timestamp alone: two events occurring close together are not necessarily the same action.

### Keep explanations narrow
A history can support reconciliation of recorded movements. It does not automatically prove that every physical movement was recorded or that all external channels use the same stock system.

For an illustrative count of ten pieces followed by a subtraction of two, an ending record of eight is arithmetically consistent. Whether the two pieces were genuinely dispatched requires operational evidence beyond that arithmetic.

### Make the next review easier
Use meaningful adjustment notes and consistent item identities. Keep customer-sensitive information out of inventory explanations. If a record looks wrong, preserve the evidence before making another correction.

This article should sit within the existing stock-history content cluster, not compete with it for an identical setup query.

title: Choosing a store template is different from changing your store content
body:
A template establishes a presentation structure. It does not supply accurate merchant information just because its preview looks complete.

### Three separate decisions
The inspected oBizee template screen loads its available catalogue and separates design selection from content and brand-colour editing. It also includes unavailable and empty-catalogue states. A screenshot of a design is not evidence that it is selectable for every store at every moment.

Choose a structure around the information customers need to evaluate your products. Then check your own copy and photographs inside it. Finally inspect the colours on important controls and text.

### Evaluate with real catalogue shapes
A long product title, a portrait photograph and a missing optional field reveal different problems from a short title and a perfect demonstration image. Include those cases in your evaluation. Check the bag and checkout as well as the homepage.

### Avoid a false promise
No template can guarantee a sales increase. A useful selection makes your products understandable and the next action clear without misrepresenting the catalogue.

Use the template-selection capability page for the supported controls. Keep the exact available catalogue and any rollout announcement tied to current deployment evidence rather than an old design inventory.

title: Three brand colours still need a readability check
body:
Choosing brand colours is not simply finding three shades that look attractive together. The colours have jobs: communicating actions, supporting emphasis and highlighting smaller details.

### What the editor exposes
The inspected brand-colour screen provides primary, secondary and accent values, checks the entered colour format and sends a save request. A valid hex value proves only that the value can be interpreted. It does not prove readable contrast in every rendered component.

Keep the main action recognisable when you apply your palette. Check text over light and dark surfaces, badges, disabled controls and focus indicators. A logo colour may be useful as a small accent without being suitable behind paragraph text.

### Test content states
Inspect an actual long product name and a real error message, not only an empty preview. A colour that works in a large heading can be difficult to read in smaller supporting text.

### Keep claims proportionate
Changing colours does not establish accessibility compliance, conversion improvement or a complete custom design. Those outcomes require broader checks.

The feature page explains the available controls; the help article owns saving instructions. This piece addresses why a technically valid colour choice still needs a customer-facing readability review.

title: Homepage editing should answer a buyer’s question before adding another section
body:
More homepage content is not automatically more useful content. A section earns its space by answering a buying question or helping someone reach a relevant product.

### Begin with existing facts
The inspected merchant application includes a website content-editing surface. That is evidence of editing capability, not evidence that every template supports the same sections or that every saved field is visible in every layout.

Prepare a clear offer, representative product images and a practical next step. If you do not have an approved customer quotation, leave out the testimonial claim rather than filling a design slot with invented praise.

### Review the whole journey
After changing content, check where the main action leads. A headline promising a collection should not send people to an unrelated item. Confirm that the destination still contains the products the homepage describes.

Read the mobile version from top to bottom. Look for repeated information, missing context and important details pushed below decorative material.

### Know the boundary
Editing copy does not change inventory, delivery capacity or payment availability. The words must match those operational facts.

The homepage-content feature page owns capability evaluation and the help guide owns the controls. The editorial lesson is to make each section do a distinct job without confusing a richer layout with a stronger promise.

title: Store text assistance should leave the merchant in control
body:
Assisted wording can reduce the blank-page problem, but it should not obscure who is responsible for the final claim.

### What the inspected implementation says
The current source displays a merchant-facing explanation that store wording is generated from products and photographs at the first, fifth and tenth product milestones, then stops. It also states that merchant-edited wording is not changed and provides a switch. The control is disabled for unsupported designs.

These are source-verified implementation statements. Before publishing them as a release announcement, match the app and backend rollout and test a supported store. An implementation date is not a customer availability date.

### What the merchant should review
Check materials, quantities, delivery language and product identity in any generated wording. An attractive sentence can still imply a guarantee you do not offer. Correct the actual meaning, not only spelling.

### What the feature is not
Do not describe this as an unlimited marketing agent, automated SEO success or permission to invent reviews. The inspected surface describes a bounded wording process.

This explainer belongs with homepage-copy controls. A separately dated release note should be published only when its deployment and observed behaviour are documented.

title: A live-store switch is a visibility decision, not a readiness certificate
body:
A store can be visible before it is ready to be promoted. Treat changing visibility and completing a launch check as separate decisions.

### What the control establishes
The inspected application includes a website live-toggle component. Its existence supports explaining a visibility control, not claiming that activating it validates prices, delivery coverage or payment setup.

Before sending traffic, inspect a representative product, its options, the bag and the delivery step. Check that contact and store information are accurate. If the payment flow depends on merchant confirmation, explain that workflow rather than suggesting automatic reconciliation.

### Avoid the circular check
Seeing the homepage load proves the homepage loads. It does not prove an order can be processed correctly. Use an authorised test workflow when verifying a transaction; do not create real orders casually to test copy.

### Keep an operational record
Record which store and setting you changed and what you checked afterward. If visibility must be reversed, understand the supported control before making the change.

This is a launch-readiness explainer within the homepage feature cluster. It should not become a duplicate step-by-step toggle guide or an unsupported promise that one switch completes every launch requirement.

title: A delivery fee is a store rule, not a courier quotation
body:
The amount a store charges a customer and the amount a courier charges the merchant are different figures. Confusing them can make an apparently simple delivery setting misleading.

### What the settings cover
The inspected delivery screen exposes standard pricing, an optional faster tier, a free-shipping threshold and estimated delivery windows. These are merchant configuration controls. Their presence does not establish a negotiated carrier rate, guaranteed transit time or courier coverage for every address.

Choose the customer charge from your actual operating model. If you subsidise delivery, account for that in the order economics rather than assuming the cost disappears.

### Check boundaries
Inspect a bag below the threshold, at the threshold and above it in an authorised test setup. Check the fast option separately if offered. Verify the customer sees the intended fee and wording.

### Keep the promise consistent
A checkout note that mentions an old threshold can contradict the configured rule. Update explanatory text when the policy changes, and distinguish an estimate from a delivery commitment.

Use the delivery-rules feature page for available settings and the help guide for editing. This explanation concerns the meaning of the fee, not a recommendation for a specific shipping price.

title: Pincode rules express where you choose to take orders
body:
A delivery area should describe a promise you can fulfil. A list of accepted pincodes is not evidence that every courier can serve them.

### What the form exposes
The inspected delivery screen provides serviceable and blocked pincode lists. Its help text describes comma-separated six-digit entries and says that leaving the serviceable list blank allows delivery everywhere. Treat that as a consequential setting, not a harmless empty field.

Before saving, prepare the areas you actually intend to accept. Do not infer precedence between conflicting entries without testing the current runtime. Remove contradictory rules rather than relying on an undocumented assumption.

### Verify representative addresses
Check one intended serviceable pincode and one excluded pincode in an authorised test flow. If the interface presents an unexpected result, investigate before promoting delivery availability.

### Understand the limit
A pincode rule is a storefront eligibility rule. It does not guarantee carrier pickup, delivery dates, parcel acceptance or a live carrier quotation. Keep those checks in the fulfilment process.

This article belongs with delivery rules rather than a new broad shipping guide. Its distinctive purpose is explaining the difference between store-defined order eligibility and external courier serviceability.

title: A requested delivery date is a preference until you confirm it
body:
Gift buyers often care about a date, not just a delivery speed. Asking for that date can be useful without promising that every selected date is achievable.

### What the control does
The inspected settings include an option to show or hide the requested-delivery-date picker. The wording describes the date as the customer’s preference. That is materially different from a guaranteed arrival appointment.

When evaluating the feature, check whether the chosen date appears in the order information you use operationally. Confirm the business can review that request before making a commitment.

### Explain the response
If a requested date cannot be met, communicate an actual alternative. Do not leave the customer to infer acceptance from the mere presence of the date in checkout. Keep production time, dispatch time and transit estimates distinct.

### Avoid overstating the capability
A date field is not a production-capacity calendar, courier reservation or service-booking confirmation. Those require separate evidence.

Use the requested-delivery-date feature page for supported scope. This explainer helps merchants choose honest language around the field and helps buyers understand what they are asking for. It is not a claim that the platform can guarantee arrival for an occasion.

title: Checkout notes explain delivery rules; they do not create them
body:
A checkout note is useful for a short explanation the customer needs at that moment. It becomes dangerous when it describes a rule the store has not actually configured.

### What the source supports
The inspected delivery settings include a note shown on the delivery step. Pricing and pincode controls appear separately. This separation matters: writing “free delivery above a threshold” in a note is not evidence that the threshold rule is active.

Keep the note aligned with the saved settings. Prefer one practical message over a long collection of policies that becomes hard to scan on a phone.

### Use a consistency check
Choose a representative bag and inspect the displayed charge beside the note. Check whether the text still makes sense when a faster option is selected or the address is outside the intended area.

### Keep exceptions explicit
If handmade production takes additional time, do not hide that constraint behind a cheerful delivery slogan. Use accurate wording and the appropriate product or policy surface for detail.

This article should support the existing delivery-rules page, not become another generic checkout checklist. Its specific lesson is that explanatory copy and operational configuration must agree.

title: UPI details explain where to pay, not whether payment arrived
body:
Showing a UPI ID or bank details gives a buyer a destination for a direct payment. It does not establish that the transfer succeeded.

### What the merchant interface says
The inspected payout-details screen explains a flow for stores without a payment gateway: the customer places an order, sees the details and pays from their own app. It explicitly tells the merchant to confirm receipt in their own bank or UPI app before accepting the order.

The same source includes a locked state when secure server storage is unavailable. Do not promise universal availability simply because the fields exist in the code.

### Separate the evidence
A customer reference or screenshot is a claim to investigate, not a substitute for checking the actual receiving account. Compare the intended order and amount with the funds received through your normal authorised process.

### What this does not promise
Direct-pay details are not automated bank reconciliation, a payout timetable or a gateway integration. Avoid language suggesting that every displayed payment claim is already verified.

Use the direct-pay feature page for the supported workflow. A release announcement about these controls still requires matching deployed app/backend evidence and an authorised account test.

title: Confirming payment and accepting an order are different decisions
body:
Receiving money answers one question. Accepting the order answers another: can you fulfil the agreed items and conditions?

### What changed in the implementation
The inspected merchant commit 3f1bab2 introduces a direct-payment strip and separates confirmation from acceptance. Its description explains why the order remains available after confirmation: the merchant still needs to act on it. This is implementation evidence, not a declaration of a public launch date.

### Use the separation deliberately
First verify the direct payment through the actual receiving account. Then check the product, quantity and fulfilment commitment before accepting. A customer’s payment screenshot alone should not collapse those checks into a single assumption.

If payment is not found, retain the distinction between an unresolved claim and an accepted order. Use the available workflow rather than inventing a status in a message.

### Bound the claim
This explanation does not promise automatic bank checking, availability for every payment method or a particular refund process. Those are separate capabilities.

The order-workspace page owns the broader feature description. This article explains the operational value of keeping two decisions separate. Publish a dated release note only once the corresponding deployment and account behaviour have been verified.

title: An order workspace helps you separate money from fulfilment
body:
An order can be awaiting money, awaiting dispatch or awaiting a customer decision. Describing all of those situations simply as “pending” makes the next action harder to identify.

### What the inspected surfaces support
The merchant order workspace has separate navigation and dedicated money and delivery components. That supports an explanation of distinct operational views. It does not imply that every displayed status is automatically updated by an external system.

Start with the question you need to answer. Use the money information to understand recorded amounts and the delivery information to understand fulfilment. Reconcile contradictory evidence instead of assuming one summary label explains everything.

### Keep a clear next action
For an illustrative order with a recorded balance and no shipment, decide whether payment follow-up or fulfilment preparation comes first under your process. Do not treat opening a tab as performing the action.

### Avoid feature inflation
An organised workspace is not proof of universal courier integration, automated accounting or guaranteed notification delivery. Describe those only where verified separately.

Link this explanation to the existing order-workspace capability page and task-specific help. Its role is to explain the decision structure, not duplicate every button label in a second manual.

title: A recorded balance is not a bank statement
body:
Order money records are useful because they keep the order’s financial picture together. They should still be read as records, not independent confirmation from a bank.

### What is displayed
The inspected Money tab shows items, delivery charge, discount, total, paid and due amounts, with an action for clearing the due amount when applicable. It also includes the order’s bill surface. These are distinct pieces of information.

Before changing a recorded balance, confirm what actually happened. Was money received, an amount waived, or a record entered incorrectly? Those are different explanations even if they produce the same final due amount.

### Preserve the distinction
A zero displayed balance does not by itself prove a transfer reached the intended account. Likewise, a generated document does not independently validate payment. Use authorised receiving-account evidence for a direct payment.

### A practical review
Compare the order total, recorded paid amount and due amount. Investigate inconsistency before making another entry. Avoid placing unnecessary bank or customer information in notes.

The balance-records feature page covers the capability. This explainer focuses on interpreting the numbers responsibly and does not provide tax, accounting or settlement guarantees.

title: Generating a bill and downloading an existing bill are separate actions
body:
A document attached to an order should have a clear identity. Repeatedly creating documents when you only wanted another copy can make later reconciliation confusing.

### What the order interface distinguishes
The inspected Money tab shows an existing document number and document type with a download action when a document exists. Otherwise it presents a not-yet-generated state and a generation action.

That distinction is useful operationally. First determine whether the document already exists. Then obtain the existing copy or follow the supported generation workflow. Do not infer replacement or cancellation rules from the presence of a download button.

### Review the contents
Check the customer and order identity, items and recorded amounts before sending a document. A successful PDF download proves file delivery, not that every field is correct.

### Keep claims limited
This source evidence does not establish statutory compliance for every merchant, universal GST treatment or automatic accounting-system integration. Those depend on configuration and appropriate professional requirements.

The bill-document feature page owns supported capability and related help owns the procedure. This explainer answers the narrower question of when someone needs a document created and when they only need the document already on record.

title: A tracking link is a way to find updates, not proof of delivery
body:
A customer asking “Where is my order?” needs the best available status and a meaningful next step. A tracking link helps them reach updates, but the link alone does not prove delivery.

### What the inspected interface offers
The delivery component includes tracking information, copying or opening a link and provider-dependent label handling. It explicitly distinguishes point-to-point delivery without a printed label and advises checking the courier for the latest status.

Do not assume every provider uses the same label or tracking workflow. Confirm which information belongs to the actual shipment before sharing it.

### Check the destination
Open the intended tracking destination and verify that it relates to the correct shipment. Avoid sharing private internal links or another customer’s record.

### Explain uncertainty honestly
If a carrier has not updated its status, say what is known and what you are checking. Do not convert “label created” into “dispatched” or “dispatched” into “delivered” without supporting evidence.

The tracking feature page is the capability owner. This article explains what tracking information means and does not promise real-time updates, guaranteed delivery dates or support for every courier.

title: Order lookup and customer order history solve different problems
body:
A buyer trying to locate one order has a different task from a buyer reviewing their purchases with a store. Keeping those tasks distinct helps avoid confusing access instructions.

### The inspected distinction
The order-tracking page asks for an order number and an email or phone number. The separate My Orders page uses the checkout email and a one-time-code flow before displaying the customer’s orders. These are source observations, not proof of a completed live authentication test.

Use the single-order route when the buyer has the relevant reference and needs that order’s status. Use the account-style history route for the supported collection of orders associated with the checkout identity.

### Do not request more data than needed
Customer support should guide the buyer toward the appropriate interface rather than asking them to send OTPs or unnecessary personal details in a public message. A code is for the authentication flow, not a support quotation.

### Keep expectations precise
This is not a promise of cross-store purchase history or recovery of orders under every different email address. The owning customer-history feature page should describe the supported scope, while the help articles provide the exact steps and troubleshooting.

title: Service-request details should not be mistaken for a confirmed appointment
body:
Collecting information about a service request can help the merchant assess it. It does not necessarily mean a time slot has been reserved or the work accepted.

### What the source establishes
The inspected storefront includes a dedicated service-booking step. That is evidence of a service-related checkout surface. The title of a component is not enough to claim calendar synchronisation, real-time capacity checks or guaranteed appointments.

Describe the information requested in terms the merchant can actually fulfil. If a customer provides a preferred time, explain whether the merchant must confirm it. Keep this separate from a promise of instant booking.

### Evaluate with a real service shape
Use an authorised test case reflecting the details the business needs, such as the requested service and scheduling information. Inspect how those details appear for follow-up. Do not submit a live request merely to obtain a screenshot without permission.

### State the boundary
A request form can organise an enquiry while leaving acceptance and scheduling to a later workflow. Marketing should not erase that distinction.

The service-request feature page owns this capability. A stronger booking claim should wait for verified end-to-end behaviour, not be inferred from a field or component name.

title: A saved bag is convenient, but it is not a reserved order
body:
A buyer may add products, leave and return later. Remembering a bag can make that journey easier without guaranteeing that every earlier selection is still available at its earlier price.

### What to distinguish
The inspected V1 storefront has a cart context and cart view. Those surfaces organise selected items and quantities. They are not, by themselves, evidence of stock reservation, cross-device synchronisation or an accepted order.

Treat the bag as the customer’s current intention. Checkout is where the current buying conditions need to be resolved. Do not tell customers that an item is secured merely because it appears in a saved list.

### Evaluate the return journey
In an authorised test, add a product, change its quantity and return to the bag. Check the current product identity and what happens when information has changed. Keep the test separate from an actual purchase.

### Communicate the next step
A clear bag should show what the customer intends to buy and how to continue. If something is unavailable, the message should help them resolve it rather than implying the order already exists.

This explainer belongs in the existing store-versus-messaging cluster. It should not duplicate the whole cart help guide or promise persistence beyond the verified environment.
